ONGOING R&D / MUJOCO SIMULATION

Hybrid Embodied AI for Dual-Arm Manipulation

I’m using Python to integrate GRIT manipulation policies with a C++ RMPflow motion executor for the dual-arm Rainbow RB-Y1 in MuJoCo. The project explores how learned policies and model-based control can work together during coordinated manipulation and contact with objects.

01 / SIMULATION INTEGRATION

Connecting policy and control

My current focus is the interface between GRIT and RMPflow. I’m investigating how closely the simulated robot follows the policy’s commands and how contact dynamics and execution constraints affect tracking.

RB-Y1 / SIMULATION DEMO

Coordinating the bottle and cup

02 / TASK REASONING

Reasoner on Mac mini M4

I developed the project’s Reasoner on a Mac mini M4. This is the task reasoning layer, where I’m exploring how to use scene context to propose manipulation steps.

I’m designing the perception pipeline around RGB-D observations, object segmentation, and geometric scene representations. Connecting those inputs to the Reasoner and passing its task plans to the motion executor are integration goals.

03 / PUBLISHED HARDWARE RESEARCH

Related work on the UR10

In a separate study, I evaluated RMPflow-Magnetic on a physical UR10 equipped with end-of-arm radar. The C++ reactive policy used radar range and Doppler closing speed to steer around obstacles while preserving motion toward the goal. The experiments included moving transparent obstacles.
